label: def:typed-garside-element
title: Typed Garside element of the nuclear braid
html:
Definition. Let \mathcal{A}(Z, N) be a nucleus with A = Z + N nucleons in ordering (t_0, \ldots, t_{A-1}) where t_i \in \{p, n\}. The typed Garside element is the element \mathcal{G}(t_0, \ldots, t_{A-1}) \in H_A(q) built by the Garside staircase with typed crossings.

Construction. The Garside staircase has A - 1 levels. At level \ell, strand \ell + 1 crosses all earlier strands from right to left. Each crossing is typed by the nucleon pair (t_j, t_{\ell+1}):

\mathcal{G}(t_0, \ldots, t_{A-1})
  \;=\;
  \prod_{\ell=0}^{A-2}
  \;\prod_{j=\ell}^{0}
  C(t_j,\, t_{\ell+1};\, \sigma_j),

where C(f_i, f_j; \sigma_k) = \sigma_k + d(f_i, f_j) is the typed crossing operator with coefficients:

  d(p, p) = 0, \qquad
  d(n, n) = -(q - q^{-1}), \qquad
  d(p, n) = d(n, p) = -\tfrac{1}{2}(q - q^{-1}).

The product contains \binom{A}{2} factors. The result is reduced to Gröbner–Shirshov normal form under the braiding-induced ordering.

Archimedean specialisation. What follows sits on the archimedean side of the substrate wall. It invokes real- or complex-analytic constructs. Any generic categorical identities it draws on remain valid over an abstract coefficient ring; only their archimedean realisation is specialised here.
